evidence_items.explanation: WILDS reports performance losses across ten datasets involving natural distribution shifts. This supports recurring generalization difficulty across applications, without establishing a universal inability.

The paper identifies a concrete extrapolation failure for a common graph-network configuration. It also shows that suitable architectural choices and training distributions can permit successful extrapolation.

receipt.public_excerpt: as an indicator of generalization performances

evidence_items.explanation: The authors show why high-dimensional learning commonly occurs outside the training points' convex hull. This challenges a literal geometric reading, but does not establish reliable performance under distribution shifts.

A neural network trained for compositional skills demonstrates successful systematic generalization. This limits any universal interpretation, while remaining compatible with difficulty under conventional training.

unresolved_gaps: The evidence does not establish a single geometric boundary beyond which neural networks generally fail.
The selected studies are not a census of every architecture used during the three decades.
